User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the BlogVista platform, primarily for authentication and authorship of blog content.

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity.

email.description: The unique email address of the user.

passwordHash.description: The securely hashed password for user authentication, managed by the authentication system.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the user account was created.

Blog.title: Blog
Blog.description: Represents a blog post created by a user, including its content, publication status, and an optional AI-generated summary.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Blog entity.

userId.description: Reference to the User who authored this blog post. (Relationship: User 1:N Blog)

title.description: The title of the blog post.

slug.description: A unique, URL-friendly identifier for the blog post, typically derived from its title.

content.description: The main rich-text content of the blog post.

summary.description: A concise, AI-generated summary of the blog post content. This field is optional.

isPublished.description: A flag indicating whether the blog post is publicly visible.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the blog post was originally created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the blog post was last updated.

Like.title: Like
Like.description: Records an authenticated user's 'like' on a specific blog post. A unique constraint ensures a user can like a post only once.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Like entity.

userId.description: Reference to the User who performed the like. (Relationship: User 1:N Like)

blogId.description: Reference to the Blog post that received the like. (Relationship: Blog 1:N Like)

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the like was created.

Comment.title: Comment
Comment.description: Represents a user-generated comment on a specific blog post.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Comment entity.

blogId.description: Reference to the Blog post this comment is associated with. (Relationship: Blog 1:N Comment)

userId.description: Reference to the User who authored this comment. (Relationship: User 1:N Comment)

content.description: The textual content of the comment.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the comment was created.

definition.description: Root collection for user profiles. Each document ID (`userId`) corresponds to the Firebase Authentication UID. This path facilitates path-based ownership for secure access to user-specific data.

Subcollection storing all blog posts, including drafts, owned by a specific user. The `{userId}` wildcard ensures ownership is tied directly to the authenticated user. This supports private dashboard operations (create, edit, delete). Includes `userId` as an explicit owner reference.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who owns these blogs, matching `request.auth.uid`.

params.name: blogId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific blog post.

definition.description: Top-level collection containing only *published* blog posts. This collection is a denormalized view used for the public feed and public blog access, ensuring all documents are public-readable without filtering in security rules. Backend services (e.g., Cloud Functions) are responsible for synchronizing data from `/users/{userId}/blogs/{blogId}` when `isPublished` changes. Includes denormalized `userId` (author ID), and optionally denormalized `likeCount` and `commentCount` (not in schema, but required for feed).

params.name: blogId
params.description: The unique identifier for a published blog post.

definition.description: Subcollection recording a 'like' on a published blog post. The document ID (`likerUserId`) is set to the liking user's UID to enforce a unique constraint (one like per user per blog). Includes denormalized 'userId' (the liker's ID) for rule clarity, and 'blogId' is implied by the parent path.

params.name: blogId
params.description: The unique identifier of the published blog post being liked.

params.name: likerUserId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who liked the blog, used as the document ID.

definition.description: Subcollection storing comments for a published blog post. Includes `userId` (the commenter's ID) for authorization checks (e.g., for deletion) and `blogId` is implied by the parent path. Comments are sorted by `createdAt`.

params.name: blogId
params.description: The unique identifier of the published blog post receiving the comment.

params.name: commentId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific comment.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to meet the core principles of Authorization Independence, Structural Segregation, and QAPs (Queries Are Not Filters), ensuring a secure, scalable, and debuggable blog platform. 

**Authorization Independence:**
1.  **User Profiles (`/users/{userId}`):** Authorization for user profiles relies directly on `request.auth.uid` matching the `{userId}` wildcard in the path, ensuring that users can only access their own profile data. This eliminates any need for `get()` calls in security rules to determine ownership.
2.  **Private Blog Management (`/users/{userId}/blogs/{blogId}`):** Similarly, blog posts within a user's private dashboard are secured by ensuring `request.auth.uid` matches `{userId}` in the path. Furthermore, the `userId` field is explicitly stored within each blog document, allowing for robust rules like `allow write: if request.auth.uid == userId;` without resorting to `get()` calls on parent documents or other collections. This means an owner can atomically create or update their blog without checking their user status from another document.
3.  **Likes (`/public_blogs/{blogId}/likes/{likerUserId}`):** The unique document ID for a 'like' is the `likerUserId` (i.e., `request.auth.uid`). This design inherently prevents duplicate likes by the same user on the same blog and allows rules to check `request.auth.uid == likerUserId` without any `get()` operations.
4.  **Comments (`/public_blogs/{blogId}/comments/{commentId}`):** Comments include the `userId` of the author. For operations like deleting a comment, the rule can directly compare `request.auth.uid == resource.data.userId`, again avoiding `get()` calls.

**Structural Segregation & QAPs (Queries Are Not Filters):**
1.  **Public vs. Private Blogs:** The most critical aspect for QAPs is the clear segregation of blog data. 
    *   `/users/{userId}/blogs/{blogId}`: This collection stores all of a user's blogs, including drafts. Access is strictly controlled by the owner. This ensures that a query for a user's blogs (`db.collection('users').doc(userId).collection('blogs')`) will only return their own content, and security rules will not filter out unauthorized documents.
    *   `/public_blogs/{blogId}`: This is a dedicated, denormalized collection that contains *only published* blog posts. When a blog is published or unpublished from `/users/{userId}/blogs/{blogId}`, a backend process (e.g., Cloud Function) syncs the data to/from this collection. This crucial segregation allows for an extremely simple and performant security rule: `allow read: true;` on this collection, as every document within it is guaranteed to be public. This completely satisfies the QAP for the 'Public Feed' (`GET /public/feed`) and 'Public Blog Access' (`GET /public/blogs/:slug`) endpoints, as client-side queries can fetch directly without any security rule filtering.
2.  **Likes and Comments for Public Blogs:** `likes` and `comments` are placed as subcollections under `/public_blogs/{blogId}`. This ensures that likes and comments are only associated with publicly visible blogs, and allows for efficient `list` operations for a specific blog's likes or comments without security rules needing to verify the parent blog's status. For example, `db.collection('public_blogs').doc(blogId).collection('comments')` will securely retrieve all comments for that blog.

**Denormalization for Performance and Security:**
*   The `public_blogs` collection denormalizes blog data for efficient public access. It implicitly ensures `isPublished: true` for all documents within it (enforced by backend logic). This collection would also include denormalized `userId` (author's ID) and potentially denormalized `likeCount` and `commentCount` to support the 'Public Feed' requirements efficiently without needing to aggregate data at query time or perform `get()` calls in rules. While `likeCount` and `commentCount` are not explicitly in the `Blog` schema, they are critical for the 'Public Feed' and represent a best practice for denormalization in this context.
